37 A motor is required to operate at a distance of 800 m from its power supply. The motor requires a
potential difference (p.d.) of 16.0 V and a current of 0.60 A to operate.
Two wires are used to supply power to the motor as shown.
wires
power
supply
motor
800 m
The resistance of each of these wires is 0.0050 Ω per metre.
What is the minimum output p.d. of the power supply?
A
11.2 V
B
16.0 V
C
18.4 V
D
20.8 V

hints: Notice the diagram shows two separate $800 \text{ m}$ wires, one for current to the motor and one for current back, so the $0.60 \text{ A}$ passes through $1600 \text{ m}$ of wire in total.
Use resistance per metre $0.0050 \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}^{-1}$ to find the resistance of one $800 \text{ m}$ wire, then double it, then use $V = IR$ for the p.d. lost in the wires.
The supply p.d. must equal the $16.0 \text{ V}$ across the motor plus the p.d. dropped across the two wires in series with it.
walkthrough: Find the resistance of one connecting wire. $R = 800 \text{ m} \times 0.0050 \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}^{-1} = 4.0 \text{ } \Omega$.
The circuit is a series loop, so current $0.60 \text{ A}$ flows through both wires. Total wire resistance is $R_{total} = 2 \times 4.0 \text{ } \Omega = 8.0 \text{ } \Omega$.
Calculate the p.d. lost in the wires with $V = IR$. $V_{wires} = 0.60 \text{ A} \times 8.0 \text{ } \Omega = 4.8 \text{ V}$.
By conservation of energy around the loop, supply p.d. = wire drop + motor p.d. $V_{supply} = 4.8 \text{ V} + 16.0 \text{ V} = 20.8 \text{ V}$.

A.explanation: Subtracts the $4.8 \text{ V}$ lost in the wires from $16.0 \text{ V}$ instead of adding it, but the supply must be larger than the motor p.d.

B.explanation: Ignores the resistance of the $800 \text{ m}$ connecting wires and assumes no p.d. is lost between supply and $16.0 \text{ V}$ motor.

C.explanation: Includes the drop in only one $800 \text{ m}$ wire, $2.4 \text{ V}$, but the $0.60 \text{ A}$ current flows out and back through two wires.

D.explanation: Adds the $4.8 \text{ V}$ drop in both wires to the $16.0 \text{ V}$ needed by the motor to give $20.8 \text{ V}$ at the supply.
